routes.title: Switzerland: an operator-owned electricity AI fallback drill
brief: Ask Swissgrid to compare AI fallback controls with current practice in an isolated replay.
Swissgrid has not agreed; a successful simulation would not establish grid-wide resilience.
routes.impactRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a new assessment or measurement. Hide these ordinal fields for this quantitative-only card; safety impact remains unmeasured.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a probability or new assessment. The agreement inventory is incomplete and all exact-proposal consent is unknown.
routes.actor: Swissgrid AG's authorised pilot sponsor and operational owner; board and executive functions are one institution, not separate coalition partners.
routes.obligor: The consenting operator for a bounded offline pilot. An external rights holder is needed only if existing replay, data or scoring rights are insufficient.
routes.instrument: Proposed internal pilot authorisation and operational fallback appendix, with any necessary licence/data permissions. No signed pilot instrument or delegation was located.
routes.safeguard: Compare current procedures with permissioned fallback and recovery controls on preregistered matched critical faults and benign controls in an isolated simulator; never inject faults into the live grid.
routes.verification: Operator-set recovery objective, retained logs, blind scoring where possible and matched baseline. The Geneva scenario's 30 critical cases and proposed 27/30 gate are design proposals, not observed results or resource coverage.
routes.remedy: Proposed stop of the experiment for any simulated service-envelope breach pending review; reject scaling if thresholds fail or benign controls worsen. No regulatory penalty or live-grid shutdown authority inferred.
routes.window: Sector-code work is ongoing with no adoption deadline. Spring 2027 is the announced public-consultation opening target, not enactment. The 31 January 2027 selection check and February–May replay are researcher-proposed dates, not operator commitments.
routes.evidenceSummary: Swissgrid reports an in-house AI control-energy application; its governance page identifies institutional risk responsibilities but not pilot signing delegation. The Federal Council's 28 October update encourages electricity-sector voluntary work, not consent to this trial.
routes.gap: No operator consent, approved simulator boundary, baseline, delegated signatory or matched AI-facility electricity denominator. Swissgrid's production application does not prove an isolated test environment exists.
routes.nextQuestion: Can an authorised Swissgrid owner approve isolated replay, fallback, logs and independent scoring under existing rights, with a measured baseline?
incentives: Hypothesis: an operator could test recovery without risking live service and document staff workload.
constraints: Operator participation is unknown; government encouragement cannot substitute for it.
Metered coverage must use the same AI-facility population and period; national electricity or GDP shares are not substitutes.
External permissions remain conditional on the rights audit.

quantitative.coverageLimitation: No matched numerator or denominator for MWh serving the same declared AI-facility population. Proposed fault-test success is not resource-pool coverage.

agreements.scope: Swissgrid-hosted offline fallback drill under sufficient existing rights. External rights holders are conditional; optional SFOE convening is not a gate.

actors.name: Swissgrid AG
actors.role: Pilot authorisation, operational/technical ownership and rights clearance within one institution
actors.note: Merges the source graph's authorisation, operations and rights-clearance nodes. A reported production application is not acceptance of this proposal; external rights ownership remains unresolved.

limitations: Source graph resolves only one necessary institution for the chosen host. For a connected one-institution path, at least N−1 = 0 external transfers are forced; this is not proof that no outside permission is needed.
No full agreement register, delegation or exact safeguard acceptance was located. Additional rights holders must be counted if the audit establishes they are indispensable.

routes.title: UK: test staged autonomy and fallback for an energy operator
brief: Test energy AI before handing over control
Use an operator-authorised replay to compare staged autonomy and fallback with current controls.
The 6 November evidence deadline opens a policy conversation, not permission to run a trial.
routes.impactRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a new assessment or measurement. Hide these ordinal fields; safety impact remains unmeasured.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a probability or new assessment. Counterparties and required permissions remain unidentified.
routes.actor: A consenting energy operator's delegated operational and data owner. DESNZ controls strategy evidence uptake, not trial permission.
routes.obligor: The participating operator, with supplier or data-owner permissions only where existing rights do not suffice.
routes.instrument: Proposed bounded operator test authorisation and assurance/fallback protocol; separately, evidence for the DESNZ AI-enabled clean-energy strategy. No enacted safety duty is established by the call.
routes.safeguard: Replay a fixed historical workload under current and proposed staged-autonomy controls, including correlated outages and model changes; use an isolated trial only with authorisation.
routes.verification: Independently reviewed fault cases; safe fallbacks within a preregistered envelope divided by all fault episodes, with dispatch delay, workload and cost reported separately. No results are recorded.
routes.remedy: Proposed halt if usable data, an operational owner or a safe envelope is absent. Any later operating restriction requires a separately authorised instrument.
routes.window: DESNZ evidence call closes 6 November 2026; its territorial scope is England, Scotland and Wales. No strategy publication date or binding-duty deadline was located. Later operator testing is a proposal, not a booked trial.
routes.evidenceSummary: The DESNZ call asks about system-level assurance and staged autonomy while identifying fragmented data, legacy integration and vendor dependence. It provides an evidence-input opportunity, not a consented operator project.
routes.gap: Operator identity, data rights, safe envelope, current performance and consistently defined MW or MWh coverage are unknown.
routes.nextQuestion: Which operator can authorise a bounded historical replay with usable data, a baseline and enforceable fallback authority?
incentives: Hypothesis: assurance could support useful automation without compromising dispatch timing or affordability.
constraints: Do not label a strategy submission implemented regulation.
Keep simulated performance separate from live reliability and national energy coverage.
Supplier rights and policy uptake are separate conditional gates.

quantitative.coverageLimitation: The eligible asset population and covered MW or MWh have not been established. National energy capacity is not the scoped trial's resource denominator.

agreements.scope: One operator-authorised historical replay with sufficient data and fallback rights; DESNZ uptake is an optional additional policy endpoint.

actors.name: Energy operator — identity unknown

actors.note: A required institutional role from the source graph, not an identified participant. Supplier or other rights-holder consent is conditional and identities are unresolved.

limitations: The Geneva graph leaves the institution lower bound null: counterparties, rights and delegations are unresolved, so no external-transfer count is asserted.
DESNZ can accept strategy evidence but cannot substitute for the operator's trial authorisation. No complete approval denominator or accepted agreement is available.

routes.title: UK: agent permissions and accountability evidence for guidance
brief: Test limited permissions and incident records with a willing deployer, and seek incorporation of findings in ICO guidance.
The deployer and Information Commission must act separately; neither has accepted this proposal.
routes.impactRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a new assessment or measurement. Hide these fields; improved test performance would not measure catastrophic-risk reduction.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a probability or new assessment. Two necessary institutional roles are a lower bound, not a complete approval set.
routes.actor: Information Commission (operating as ICO) for guidance, and a separate consenting workflow deployer for the pilot. Commission board and executive are not separate institutions.
routes.obligor: The participating deployer under agreed pilot terms; any provider permission depends on the chosen interfaces and existing contract.
routes.instrument: Proposed pilot authorisation, minimum-permission and logging protocol, plus evidence submission and independent regulatory incorporation into data-protection guidance. Guidance is not frontier-model licensing.
routes.safeguard: Compare current controls with minimum necessary permissions and logs on synthetic personal-data workflows, including allowed and unauthorised tasks.
routes.verification: Blind reviewers reconstruct responsibility from records. Report blocked unauthorised attempts, false refusals and correct reconstructions with their separate denominators, sample sizes and uncertainty; no measured values are available.
routes.remedy: Proposed refusal of unauthorised actions and revision of inadequate controls or logs within the agreed pilot. Do not claim a new regulatory penalty or ICO endorsement.
routes.window: Agentic AI evidence call closes 20 November 2026. Guidance is targeted for spring 2027, not a specified day; publication and incorporation remain uncertain. If guidance slips, report the prototype separately.
routes.evidenceSummary: ICO seeks practical evidence on agentic AI accountability, security and responsible innovation. Its September 2026 transition establishes collective Information Commission governance. Neither the call nor the guidance plan accepts this safeguard.
routes.gap: No consenting deployer, fixed corpus, provider-rights audit or eligible-workflow denominator. General policy interest is not exact-proposal approval.
routes.nextQuestion: Can a personal-data workflow owner supply lawful test access and useful accountability records, and will ICO incorporate the tested safeguard?
incentives: Hypothesis: useful minimal records could clarify responsibility without exposing unnecessary personal data or vendor secrets.
constraints: Personal-data scope and an accountable actor must be established.
Synthetic prototype completion is separate from regulator-incorporated guidance.
Independent provider permission may be needed; no mandatory external memorandum is presumed.

quantitative.coverageLimitation: No frozen eligible-workflow population and covered-execution counts. A fraction of successful test cases would describe test performance, not policy resource coverage.

agreements.scope: Combined endpoint: regulator-incorporated guidance plus one distinct consenting deployer's workflow pilot, using existing rights where sufficient.

actors.name: Information Commission (operating as ICO)
actors.role: Approve and publish guidance incorporating the tested safeguard
actors.note: Support is for gathering accountability/security evidence, not acceptance of this proposal. Board and executive count as one institution.

actors.name: Workflow deployer — identity unknown
actors.role: Authorise personal-data task scope, pilot and lawful evidence access
actors.note: Distinct from the regulator in this combined endpoint. A separate provider is conditional on interface/contract insufficiency, not presumed necessary.

limitations: The source graph's two-institution lower bound requires at least N−1 = 1 inter-institutional evidence/decision transfer to connect the pilot to incorporated guidance; this is not a count of signatures or sequential administrative steps.

Submission or an independent prototype alone is a smaller endpoint and must not inherit this count. Provider permissions, pilot agreements and internal delegations are unresolved; exact consent remains unknown.

routes.title: Singapore: a purchaser-backed sandbox release gate
brief: Give one buyer a tested release gate
Use the voluntary sandbox to test whether a purchaser can withhold an unsafe agent release.
This is one buyer's agreed decision, not a Singapore government-wide gate or regional recognition scheme.
routes.impactRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a new assessment or measurement. Hide these fields; no deployment consequence or safety improvement is yet observed.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a probability or new assessment. Existing voluntary programme access does not establish purchaser, supplier or tester consent.
routes.actor: One selected deploying/purchasing organisation with actual release authority, a commercially selected tester and the sandbox admission authority.
routes.obligor: The purchaser's release owner; supplier/integrator duties only where agreed or covered by existing rights. The buyer may itself own the agent.
routes.instrument: Proposed purchaser release criteria, commercial testing agreement and applicable sandbox admission/publication terms. It is not a national government pass/fail instruction.
routes.safeguard: Test a document-processing agent with separate read/send permissions against synthetic sensitive records and malicious instructions; agree to withhold or constrain failing releases and retest remediation.
routes.verification: Held-out tasks with reset and retained memory; correctness and leakage separately; trace actual hold/remediate decisions. Any cross-lab replication tests reproducibility, not official mutual recognition.
routes.remedy: Proposed purchaser-authorised withholding of a failing deployment or removal of permissions, followed by remediation/retest. Without actual go/no-go authority, report a methods test only.
routes.window: Programme describes ongoing participation and completion of testing/case study within three months, not guaranteed intake. The 31 January 2027 selection check, February–April pilot and May retest are research proposals, not official booked dates.
routes.evidenceSummary: The Global AI Assurance Sandbox supports live or intended-production application testing and commercial tester selection. The October MDDI answer describes risk-calibrated limits but explicitly does not require frontier-model access. A participant case study is not independent proof of this proposed gate.
routes.gap: Purchaser identity and authority, inventory, tester/supplier consent, admission allocation, price and publication rights remain unresolved. Thirty programme applications do not measure policy coverage or successful safeguards.
routes.nextQuestion: Will a named purchaser sign and exercise a release rule, with necessary test rights and an auditable complete application inventory?
incentives: Hypothesis: a purchaser obtains application-specific assurance with an actionable remedy rather than a test report alone.
constraints: National government adoption and international recognition are distinct routes and are not claimed here.
The identity and independence of supplier and admission institutions remain unresolved.
Do not substitute programme reach or a participant's testing effort for the buyer's resource coverage.

quantitative.coverageLimitation: Neither signed-gate application count nor the purchaser's frozen eligible inventory is available; affected transaction share is also unknown. Programme footprint is not a denominator for this policy.

agreements.scope: One purchaser-backed application release decision within the existing external-assurance sandbox; no government-wide adoption or overseas recognition.

routes.title: Korea: a consented safety-case and incident-response rehearsal
brief: After verifying the operative rules, test a developer's incident evidence and mitigation workflow on fictional cases.
The consultation is closed and current applicability is unresolved; a drill is neither legal approval nor a new lawmaking window.
routes.impactRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a new assessment or measurement. Hide these fields; a fictional drill does not establish compliance or reduced incident risk.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Provisional 2/2 legacy-schema compatibility only, not a probability or new assessment. Final notice, enforcement position, applicability and a consenting developer remain unresolved.
routes.actor: A consenting developer's authorised safety/compliance owner; an evaluator reviews evidence. MSIT's role depends on the operative legal instrument and any separately agreed feedback.
routes.obligor: The participating developer for a voluntary rehearsal. Statutory duties cannot be inferred from the unverified draft alone.
routes.instrument: Proposed confidential voluntary drill authorisation and current-law applicability review, not a new statute or reciprocal evaluation recognition agreement.
routes.safeguard: Rehearse detection, triage, evidence preservation and reporting preparation for fictional incidents and model changes; independently repeat one mitigation test.
routes.verification: Compare baseline written policy and rehearsed workflow on matched unseen cases; score complete correctly routed evidence against verified applicable deadlines, with raw counts and evaluator agreement. Never send a false incident to authorities.
routes.remedy: Proposed correction and retest of incomplete evidence or mitigation. Stop statutory compliance claims if operative law or applicability cannot be established; retain optional research-only results separately.
routes.window: The notice consultation closed 26 February 2026. 22 January 2027 is only the earliest anniversary of an at-least-one-year enforcement grace, not a confirmed enforcement change. No live revision is established. February–April 2027 rehearsal dates are a research proposal.
routes.evidenceSummary: The retained draft describes risk-management and incident-evidence duties; the commencement announcement describes a minimum grace period and industry-promotion emphasis. Neither verifies the latest operative notice or a new 2027 consultation.
routes.gap: Final notice, subsequent amendments, latest enforcement position, in-scope developer, receipt channel and model inventory remain unverified.
routes.nextQuestion: What operative duties apply to a willing developer, and can it authorise a confidential synthetic rehearsal against those duties?
incentives: Hypothesis: rehearsed evidence could reveal operational gaps without misrepresenting a draft as law or exposing sensitive model information publicly.
constraints: Keep this voluntary developer drill distinct from the existing regional procurement and mutual-evaluation proposals.
No legislative-window, universal Korean coverage or official certification claim.
If law or developer consent is missing, do not promise pre-Geneva operational validation.

quantitative.coverageLimitation: Both verified-current-evidence model versions and the participating developer's complete in-scope model inventory are unknown. Proposed drill-event success does not supply resource coverage.

agreements.scope: A voluntary developer-owned synthetic safety-case rehearsal after checking operative law; any statutory submission or MSIT feedback is a separate conditional endpoint.

actors.note: The source graph requires evaluator review but does not establish a separate evaluator institution; do not count the internal compliance owner and developer separately. MSIT is conditional on a statutory endpoint, not a required participant in fictional drills.
